jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM The Software Integration Environment (SIE) team builds the platform Anduril uses to test software the way it will actually be flown, driven, and fought: real binaries, running on real services, under conditions we control. We provision isolated, reproducible environments for simulation and integration testing at scale, across AWS, Azure, and on-premise. The platform is used both internally by Anduril engineers and externally by our customers. Compute was the first half of that problem. The second half is the simulated world those binaries run inside — how it gets authored, how heterogeneous simulators agree on it, and how an engineer inspects and trusts what happened during a run. That is what this role owns. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer with deep C++ and real-time systems experience to build the simulation layer of the SIE platform. This is a systems software role: you will design and write the services that let independent simulators share one world — a common clock, a common entity namespace, and a clear model of who owns what — and the tooling that lets users author, reuse, and debug the scenarios they run. This is a new area with a wide surface. You will be one of the first engineers on it, which means you will set the technical direction, make the architectural calls, and be accountable for them. jobs.description_text: About The Team The Sentry Tower Software team develops robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice’s common operating picture. About the Job Sentry Towers are deployed to secure perimeters, some in contexts where the tower itself is a sensitive asset and physical access by an adversary is a realistic threat. That makes product security a hardware-and-software problem, not a policy exercise: if someone can pull a drive, attach a serial cable, plug in USB, or interrupt the bootloader, the design has to hold. We’re hiring a Senior Software Engineer to own product security for the tower platform. You’ll own the trusted boot chain top to bottom, on NVIDIA Jetson compute across several generations. That means signed firmware and bootloaders, UEFI Secure Boot, signed kernel images, encrypted root filesystems, and the key management that makes it real: hardware-security-module-backed signing keys, separate development and production trust roots, and the release pipeline that signs what we ship. jobs.description_text: Anduril Maritime builds autonomous underwater/surface vehicles: autonomy computers running control and mission logic, payload computers driving sonar and other sensors, surface integration units, and ground control stations. We're past the "does it work in the lab" phase - vehicles are in the field, and field vehicles find bugs the lab never does. We need someone whose job, starting day one, is to pick up those bugs and actually close them: reproduce it, find the real cause, fix it, ship it, tell the team what happened. To be clear about what this isn't: it's not a ticket-triage-and-forward job, and it's not "junior dev does the boring work while senior devs build features." You'll be shipping real fixes in the real codebase. You're just entering the codebase through "this broke on a vehicle" instead of "here's a clean feature spec." Once you've built up cross-subsystem fluency - which this role forces faster than sitting in one subsystem ever would - you move into owning subsystems and roadmap work like anyone else. What you'll actually be doing Take a field-reported anomaly (sensor stopped publishing, mission faulted mid-track, data stream drifted for no obvious reason) and figure out what subsystem it's actually in - not just where it was reported. Reproduce it for real. Replay recorded sensor/mission data through the live pipeline, pull it into visualization tooling, don't guess. jobs.title: Unit 26 - Software & System Architect Opportunities
jobs.description_text: Build the 26th We promise the world 25 new products a year. Unit 26 builds the 26th: SharkNinja itself. Inside a company moving as fast as ours, the highest-impact work doesn’t always fit neatly into anyone’s job description. It sits between functions and stays unsolved until someone owns it completely, builds the solution, proves its value, and ships it. That’s where Unit 26 comes in. Unit 26 is a small team of builders reporting to the Chief of Staff to the CEO, with executive sponsorship and access to the C-suite from day one. Our job is to solve problems that don’t have an obvious owner or an existing solution. When your build ships, you hand it to the business unit waiting on the other side and move to the next one. Zero to one, again and again. We’re starting with just eight builders, from inside SharkNinja and out. The Role You’ll work directly with teams across SharkNinja to understand what needs to change and what a successful solution must deliver. Then you own the build. What you make will flex with the problem: an app, an algorithm, an AI agent that eliminates thousands of hours of manual work, or a system that doesn’t yet exist at SharkNinja, or anywhere else. Some of your work will change how we run the company. Some will end up inside our products. Some will be things we haven’t imagined yet. Here, the building comes first. You’ll build on top of a global innovation engine that reaches tens of millions of homes, and you’ll have a stake in the value you create.
